rulings.evidence: REFUSED the bread near-miss: the bread commodity is a $1.69 sandwich loaf, a different product and price class from a bakery sourdough, and the vocabulary already splits Rye Bread from Sandwich Bread, so variety splits are the standing convention here. No sourdough id exists in any namespace; new id proposed.

Salted and unsalted butter are the same price class and the same macros, and the pre-resolver itself settled an unsalted butter line onto [butter] elsewhere in this same batch. The peanut-butter near-miss is a token artifact.
Extra-virgin is the grade the olive-oil commodity is captured at across the board; same food, same price class, no gram-weight difference. 13.5 g/tbsp.

REFUSED chicken-breast (boneless skinless): a split bone-in breast sells well below the boneless per-lb price AND carries about 28% bone, so bridging it would misprice and misweigh at once - the leg-quarters-are-not-thighs precedent. The estate already splits bone-in thigh and drumstick from their boneless rows. New id proposed.
Fresh, not dried - a form flip that is both a different price class and roughly a threefold difference in strength per gram. fresh-thyme is a live id at 4 of 7 stores.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Searched by food across all four namespaces for sourdough and every obvious variant (sour dough, artisan loaf, bakery bread): nothing carries it. What exists is bread (label 'Sandwich Bread', a $1.69 sliced loaf, 4 of 7 stores) and rye-bread - and that pair is itself the precedent, because the estate already treats a bread VARIETY as its own id rather than folding it into the sandwich loaf. A bakery sourdough loaf runs two to three times the sandwich-loaf price, so folding this line into bread would underprice a card whose whole selling point is being cheap. Macros also differ (281 vs 266 cal per 100 g), though that is the lesser reason.

Checked by food, not string, across all four namespaces: chicken-breast is explicitly the BONELESS SKINLESS product (7 of 7, $1.99 at Hy-Vee), rotisserie-chicken is cooked, whole-chicken is the entire bird, and no split-breast or bone-in-breast id exists under any spelling (searched split chicken breast, bone-in breast, chicken breast halves). The estate has already ruled this exact question the other way round for the dark meat: on 2026-08-24 it minted Bone-In Skinless Chicken Thigh and Bone-In Skinless Chicken Drumstick rows precisely because a bone-in cut is a different price class and cannot share the boneless row's grams. Split breasts typically sell at roughly half the boneless per-pound price and carry about 28% bone, so this is a genuine second food, not a spelling of the first.

registrar_rulings.reason: No sourdough id, label, or crown exists in commodities.json, recipe-commodities.json, the recipe board, or the live feed - the nearest rows are bread (crown 'Corner Store Bread Original White', $1.69) and french-bread (crown 'French Bakery Bread Loaf', $1.25), neither of which is a sourdough product, while real ad items ('Bakery-fresh sourdough bread $4.99', Aldi 'Sliced Sourdough Round') show the variety sells under its own name at 2-3x the sandwich loaf, matching the rye-bread variety precedent. REQUIRED EDITS with the mint: (1) add 'sourdough' to the exclude lists of bread and french-bread, whose includes (\bbread\b, 'bakery bread loaf') would otherwise claim sourdough products; (2) add allowlist pairs sourdough-bread/bread and sourdough-bread/french-bread with reason 'distinct bread variety, 2-3x price' so the audit never re-flags them; (3) namespace is recipe-only (recipe-board baseline + recipe-commodities.json, since sourdough appears in weekly ads and can go on sale); (4) build its include/exclude at neighboring-commodity rigor (~150 excludes - at minimum crumb/crust/pizza/english muffin/pretzel/starter/mix/dough); (5) SEPARATELY, the ingredient vocabulary needs a new row 'Sourdough Bread' -> sourdough-bread - it is not a rename of Sandwich Bread.

No bone-in/split breast id exists in any namespace: commodities.json's only breast ids are chicken-breast (label 'Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast', whose exclude list explicitly rejects 'bone[\s-]*in' and 'split' at lines 34-35, so its 7/7 $1.99 Hy-Vee row can never price this cut) and canned-chicken; recipe-commodities.json has only boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh; the recipe board, smp-feed (only 'bone' ids are boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh and boneless-beef-short-ribs; the lone 'Split' in the feed is fork-split English muffins), floor-id-map, and dupe-allowlist all come up empty. The id is not new to the estate: staples500/approved.json already vetted this exact id as 'Bone-In Split Chicken Breast' (lb, agent-2) with the note that the boneless matcher excludes it, and 2026-08-24's Bone-In Skinless Chicken Thigh/Drumstick rulings set the precedent that bone-in is a different price class (~28% bone, roughly half the boneless $/lb — pricing it off chicken-breast would overcharge the recipe ~2x). FOLLOW-UPS: (1) mint via add-commodity-rule.ps1 in the recipe-only namespace (recipe-board baseline; promote to weekly staples later per the staples500 slate), unit lb, include patterns requiring bone-in|split alongside chicken breast, and build the exclude list to neighboring rigor (start from chicken-breast's ~150: boneless, skinless-only, tender/strip/nugget/breaded/canned/cooked/thin-sliced, thigh/drumstick/wing, whole chicken); (2) add the allowlist pair bone-in-chicken-breast vs chicken-breast with reason 'same food different form: bone-in skin-on split breast vs boneless skinless, different price class' because the suffix sweep WILL flag the contained string; (3) separately, the ingredient NAME needs its own vocabulary row ('Bone-In Skin-On Chicken Breast') plus the food-macros-db transcription with a bone/skin yield factor like the 8/24 thigh (0.78) and drumstick (0.63) rows — the id ruling does not create it.

macro_cross_check.verdict: CALORIES PASS, CARBOHYDRATE FAILS, PROTEIN FLAGGED. Calories agree within 8.2%, so the portions are right. Two problems, and the carbohydrate one is the serious one: 8 oz of sourdough alone is about 120 g of carbohydrate, and with the 12 oz of onion the dish computes to 42 g per serving against the run's 35 g ceiling - the source's own published 35 sits exactly ON that ceiling, so any honest recompute pushes it over. I am reporting this rather than trimming the bread, because the croutons are the dish. The 27% protein shortfall is the same bone-yield artifact as beef-back-ribs: 61 g/serving x 4 = 244 g needs about 1.2 kg of boneless meat, which is the full as-purchased weight of a 2 1/4 lb BONE-IN order, so the source counted bone as meat. My 44.5 g is computed after removing about 28% bone.
